title: An increasing function and a logarithmic function

stimulus.title: The graph of $f$, and the function $g$
stimulus.text: The graph of the increasing function $f$ consists of four line segments through $(0, 1)$, $(2, 2)$, $(4, 4)$, $(6, 5)$ and $(8, 8)$, for $0 \le x \le 8$. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = 3\ln(x - 1) - 2$ for $x > 1$.

plot.label: Graph of the increasing function f, four line segments through (0, 1), (2, 2), (4, 4), (6, 5) and (8, 8)

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the value of $g(f(6))$. Give your answer correct to three decimal places. Show the work that leads to your answer.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the value of $f(g(e + 1))$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find every value of $x$ for which $g(x) = 0.4x$. Give each answer correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: Both solutions, each correct to three decimal places
accept: values that round or truncate to these two

parts.sample: Graph $y = 3\ln(x - 1) - 2$ and $y = 0.4x$ with $x$ up to at least $16$; they meet twice: $x \approx 4.594$ and $x \approx 14.545$.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Write the behavior of $g$ as $x$ approaches $1$ from the right, using limit notation.

rubric.point: $\lim_{x \to 1^+} g(x) = -\infty$, one-sided and with the sign

parts.sample: As $x \to 1^+$, $x - 1 \to 0^+$ and $\ln(x - 1)$ decreases without bound, so $\lim_{x \to 1^+} g(x) = -\infty$.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: The function $g$ is invertible. Write an expression for $g^{-1}(x)$.
